name: Employer of record & global payroll
one_line: Becomes the legal employer of a company's overseas staff so it can hire and pay workers anywhere without setting up a foreign entity.
sells: Acting as the legal employer or payroll agent for a company's workers in countries where it has no entity, for a per-worker monthly fee
customers: Companies hiring remote employees and contractors across borders, from startups to enterprises
suppliers: Local banks and cross-border payment rails to pay workers, plus the card networks behind contractor payouts and expense cards

revenue.metric: estimated combined revenue of the leading global EOR and cross-border payroll platforms
revenue.basis: illustrative; Deel's $1B+ ARR is the one hard data point, the other leaders are private and don't disclose
revenue.note: No clean public total exists. Deel disclosed $1B+ ARR and says it processes $22B of payroll a year; Remote, Papaya and Globalization Partners are private and don't publish revenue, and Rippling's global-payroll/EOR line is one part of a broader platform. This figure is an order-of-magnitude for the specialist global EOR/payroll segment and excludes incumbent domestic payroll providers like ADP and Gusto.

structure.why: Deel has pulled ahead on revenue and scale ($1B+ ARR, $17.3B valuation in 2025) while a cluster of well-funded rivals (Rippling, Remote, Papaya, Globalization Partners) and incumbent payroll firms moving in keep it from being a monopoly. No comparable market shares are published.
structure.hhi_note: These firms are mostly private and disclose neither comparable revenue nor market share, so no HHI is computed. They are ordered by last disclosed private valuation, which only Deel and Rippling have refreshed in 2025.

econ: An employer of record becomes the legal employer of a company's overseas staff, so a business can hire someone in another country without opening a subsidiary there. The economics are classic make-versus-buy and transaction costs: the provider turns the large fixed cost of setting up a foreign entity and mastering local labor law into a small per-worker fee, and spreads that specialized compliance work across thousands of clients, so scale and country coverage are the moat.

companies.name: Deel
companies.note: Pure-play leader. Surpassed $1B ARR in 2025, serves 37,000+ businesses and 1.5M workers across 150+ countries, and processes ~$22B of payroll a year; profitable three years running.

companies.name: Rippling
companies.note: A broad workforce platform (HR, IT, payroll, spend) with global payroll and EOR as one part; the $16.8B valuation reflects the whole company, not just its EOR line.

companies.name: Remote
companies.note: Pure-play global EOR and payroll, a close rival to Deel; last disclosed valuation was $3B+ in its 2022 round, so it isn't ranked against the 2025 marks.

companies.name: Papaya Global
companies.note: Payments-first global payroll platform that also offers EOR; last major valuation was ~$3.7B in 2021.

companies.name: Globalization Partners (G-P)
companies.note: One of the original EOR providers (founded 2012), with broad country coverage; private and does not publish current revenue.

companies.name: Velocity Global
companies.note: US-based global workforce provider; private, revenue not disclosed.

rank_basis: last disclosed private valuation (only Deel and Rippling have 2025 marks; others' last rounds were 2021-2022, so they are left unranked)
products_note: Flagship products as of Nov 2026, checked against each company's site and 2025 funding and press coverage. Valuations are from the companies' funding announcements (Business Wire, TechCrunch) or named research write-ups; these firms are private and do not publish comparable revenue, so they are ranked by last valuation, not market share.
